newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell says finds huge oil reserves offshore Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Shell says finds huge oil reserves offshore Nigeria.

text.p: Royal/Dutch Shell Group said appraisal drilling in two permits offshore Nigeria showed reserves at 2.2 billion barrels of crude oil.
A company official said on Friday that results from the Bonga and K.O. Okpere prospects in Shell's deep offshore concessions were "very encouraging".
"Results from the wells drilled from our deep offshore concessions were very encouraging," the senior Shell official told Reuters in Lagos.

He said the first well drilled in oil prospecting licence (OPL) 212, about 100 km off the coast of Warri in the midwest, showed a crude oil reserve estimated at about 575 million barrels while the second well also held reserves estimated at 700 million barrels.
"Evaluation of our other well drilled in OPL 219 indicated a reserve holding of about one billion barrels," he said.

Shell is operating in the deep offshore waters through a subsidiary company, Shell Nigeria Exploration and Production Company (SNEPCO), set up in 1991. Most of its current Nigerian operations are onshore.
Outgoing managing director of Shell Nigeria, Brian Anderson said at his valedictory news briefing this week that production from the deep offshore wells would begin before the end of this century.
British Petroleum and Statoil alliance, also players in the deep offshore area, have reported more modest results from the first phase of their drilling programme.

The companies said three discoveries were made from drilling depths of 500-800 metres but none was considered commercial. They expected to move into deeper waters, possibly to 1,500 metres, for the next phase of their programme in the middle of next year.
Shell said last year that Nigerian deep waters in total could prove to contain commercial reserves of anywhere between five and 20 billion barrels.
